article_title: Reflections on educational technology research and development
citation: Jonathan Michael Spector. (2017). Reflections on educational technology research and development. Educational Technology Research and Development. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-017-9545-y
title: Measure attainment rather than guessing: WYMIWYG and challenging goals
description: The author proposes WYMIWYG—'what you measure ... is what you will know you have attained'—arguing one should 'collect and analyze indicators and measures' rather than guess. Because students 'will perform only to the indicated measure', he recommends challenging goals with associated indicators. This connects measurement to goal-driven instruction.
requirements: Goals must be established so the extent of attainment can be determined
constraints: Students are often busy with many other interests and may perform only to the indicated measure
examples: The author invented the term WYMIWYG inspired by WYSIWYG word processors
key_sources: Jonathan Michael Spector. (2017). Reflections on educational technology research and development. Educational Technology Research and Development. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-017-9545-y
